risks: Journal on-disk format: replacing the hand encoder with prost produces identical bytes in proto3 (that is what the deleted test asserted), but the header refactor could change the layout. Existing user journals would become unreadable unless the format is kept byte-identical or old versions are read.
Unknown-key preservation in loa-config is user-visible. If codec.rs is swapped for toml_edit, comments and ordering behave differently. Keep the unknown_keys test as a guard.
Removing migration machinery means a future schema v2 must reintroduce a step function. That is cheap (a fn pointer list), but the TooNew refusal must stay.
Merging loa-adapter and loa-surface widens rebuild scope: any change to the contracts crate recompiles every adapter and surface crate. Acceptable at this workspace size.
Removing the concurrency stress tests in bus and exec reduces protection against ETXTBSY and race regressions. Keep one small deterministic concurrency test for each.

theming_seams: This cluster has no widgets, but it owns the theme setting and the contract crates. (1) Replace the closed `loa_config::Theme { System, Dark, Light }` enum (schema.rs; mapped by hand at loa-app/src/app.rs:1421-1435) with `Appearance { theme: ThemeRef(String), overrides: toml::Table }`. Config only names a theme: \"system\", \"dark\", \"light\", or later a user script path. The UI theme layer resolves the name through a `ThemeProvider` registry, so a later scripting language just registers another provider. Config never contains colors, spacing or fonts. Keep the `overrides` table opaque so the future language can store token overrides without a config schema change, which also preserves unknown keys. (2) The generic `Registry<A>` in loa-contracts should be reusable for `Registry<dyn ThemeProvider>` so theme sources plug in exactly like harness adapters. (3) Do not put any style data in loa-core's DOM schema. Presentation hints that harnesses emit stay as `x-` extension attributes and are interpreted only by the UI theme layer. (4) The config watcher/store should expose a change notification for `appearance`, so a theme script can hot-reload without the UI polling config.

abstractions: Port for the line-JSON transport: `trait Framing: Send + Sync { fn request(&self, id: u64, method: &str, params: Json) -> Json; fn classify(&self, msg: Json) -> Incoming; }` with `enum Incoming { Response { id: String, result: Result<Json, RpcError> }, Request { id: Json, method: String, params: Json }, Notification { method: String, params: Json } }`. Implementations: `JsonRpc2` (acp, codex), `OmpFrames` (omp and its chunking), `ClaudeControl` (control_request/control_response).

`struct StdioRpc<F: Framing> { fn spawn(cmd: Command, framing: F, inbound: Arc<dyn Inbound>) -> Result<(Arc<Self>, ChildGuard)>; async fn request<T: DeserializeOwned>(&self, method: &str, params: Json) -> Result<T>; fn notify(&self, method: &str, params: Json); fn respond(&self, id: Json, result: Result<Json, RpcError>); }` and `#[async_trait] trait Inbound: Send + Sync { async fn on_request(&self, method: &str, params: Json) -> Result<Json, RpcError>; fn on_notification(&self, method: &str, params: Json); fn on_closed(&self, status: Option<ExitStatus>); }`

`struct DomWriter<'a> { sink: &'a dyn PatchSink }` with `fn insert(&self, parent: NodeId, kind: ElementKind, attrs: impl IntoAttrs, text: impl Into<String>) -> Result<NodeId>; fn set(&self, node: NodeId, attr: &str, v: impl Into<Value>); fn close(&self, node: NodeId, status: impl Into<Value>); fn ext(&self, parent: NodeId, harness: &str, kind: &str, raw: &Json) -> NodeId`. Typed builders: `turn(..)`, `message(..)`, `call(..) -> (NodeId, NodeId)`, `decision(spec: DecisionSpec)`, `usage(Usage)`.

`struct TurnLedger { turn: Option<OpenTurn>, closed: bool }` with `OpenTurn { node, messages: HashMap<K, NodeId>, calls: HashMap<K, NodeId>, waiting: Vec<NodeId> }` (generic key K: harness item id). It provides `fn state(&self) -> SessionState; fn end_turn(&mut self, w: &DomWriter, status: TurnStatus); fn from_dom(dom: &Dom) -> Self; fn cancel_stale(&mut self, w: &DomWriter)`. Each harness mapper owns a TurnLedger plus only its protocol-specific state.

A protocol-mapper strategy: `trait EventMapper: Send { type Event; type Reply; fn apply(&mut self, ev: Self::Event, w: &DomWriter) -> Vec<Self::Reply>; fn answer(&mut self, decision: NodeId, a: &Answer, w: &DomWriter) -> Result<Option<Self::Reply>>; fn begin_turn(&mut self, p: &Prompt, w: &DomWriter) -> Result<NodeId>; fn ledger(&self) -> &TurnLedger; }`. The per-harness dispatch becomes a `HashMap<&'static str, fn(&mut M, Json, &DomWriter)>` table, or serde tagged enums, instead of the 60-140-line match blocks.

A generic session over a mapper: `struct DrivenSession<M: EventMapper, T: Transport> { mapper: Mutex<M>, transport: T, state: watch::Sender<SessionState> }` implementing HarnessSession's state, wait_idle, shutdown and the lock-mutate-publish pattern once. Harness-specific send, answer and set_model go through `trait HarnessOps { async fn send(&self, prompt: &Prompt) -> Result<()>; async fn interrupt(&self); async fn set_model(&self, sel: &str) -> Result<()>; }`.

A native-format codec port: `trait NativeCodec { fn import(path: &Path, sink: &dyn PatchSink) -> Result<()>; fn export(dom: &Dom, out: &Path) -> Result<()>; }` with shared `Residual` helpers (`take(obj, fields) -> Map`, `restore(node) -> Map`, `split_parts`/`join_parts`). Adapter::import and Adapter::export delegate to it once, in a blanket helper.

A harness registry: `trait HarnessFactory: Send + Sync { fn id(&self) -> &'static str; fn label(&self) -> &'static str; fn build(&self, cfg: &HarnessConfig) -> Arc<dyn Adapter>; }` plus `fn factories() -> Vec<Box<dyn HarnessFactory>>`, so loa-app iterates instead of matching on ids.
A capabilities builder: `Capabilities::builder().features([...]).decisions([...]).import_export().build()`, or `const` statics per harness, replacing the 13 struct literals.

theming_seams:
This cluster has no widgets, so it needs no theme tokens of its own. Its job is not to bake presentation decisions in, so a later theme or script layer controls them:

1) No formatted UI text in the domain. ports.rs Prompt::title and body (:95, :111) become a structured PromptView (kind, action, host, target, detail, fingerprint, previous keys). The UI turns these into text and styles them with semantic tokens such as `prompt.danger` for HostKeyChange::Changed and `prompt.warning` for approvals.

2) Status enums are the semantic hooks.
- loa_mcp::Status (Starting, Running, Error, Stopped)
- loa_sandbox::Availability (Ready, Unconfigured, Unavailable)
- loa_sandbox::RunState
- loa_remote::audit::Outcome (Ok, Error, Refused, Denied, Cancelled, TimedOut)

Each exposes a stable `fn semantic(&self) -> Semantic { Ok, Warn, Error, Muted, Busy }` or a stable string key via strum, which the UI maps through the token registry. Widgets never match variants to colors directly.

3) Tool descriptions, prompt preambles (sandbox worker PREAMBLE, bridge instructions) and provider describe() strings are content, not style. Keep them as consts in one `text.rs` per crate so a future script layer can override them through a registry if wanted.

4) Provider and tool registries (ProviderRegistry, ToolSet) expose stable kind keys (SandboxKind via strum, tool NAME consts). A theming or scripting layer can then attach icons, labels and colors by key without touching these crates.

5) Keep these crates free of iced and any UI dependency, so the token layer stays in the UI cluster.

abstractions: trait SurfaceProvider: Send + Sync { fn name(&self) -> &'static str; fn list(&self) -> Vec<SurfaceInfo>; async fn open(&self, req: &OpenRequest) -> Result<Arc<dyn Surface>>; async fn close(&self, uri: &SurfaceUri) -> Result<()>; fn shutdown(&self) -> BoxFuture<'_, ()>; } is the port SurfaceHub holds as Vec<Arc<dyn SurfaceProvider>>. BrowserProvider, DocsProvider, VncProvider and McpDeclaredProvider are adapters, which removes the Origin matches in hub.rs.
enum OpenRequest { Url(String), File(PathBuf), Endpoint { host_port: String, password: Option<String> }, Uri(SurfaceUri) } dispatches to the provider by name through a HashMap registry, not a match.

trait SurfaceTool: Send + Sync { fn name(&self) -> &'static str; fn scope(&self) -> ToolScope; fn schema(&self) -> serde_json::Value; async fn call(&self, hub: &SurfaceHub, args: Value) -> ToolResult; } with a ToolRegistry { tools: Vec<Box<dyn SurfaceTool>> } that serves both HostTools and the rmcp endpoint. Schemas come from #[derive(schemars::JsonSchema)] on the arg structs, so no hand-written json! blocks.

trait Capture: Send + Sync { fn frames(&self) -> broadcast::Receiver<Arc<Frame>>; fn request_keyframe(&self); async fn resize(&self, w: u32, h: u32) -> Result<()>; fn stop(&self); } is the browser feed strategy, with impls Screencast (CDP) and X11Display (Xvfb + x11rb).

struct FrameFeed { tx: broadcast::Sender<Arc<Frame>>, seq: AtomicU64, last_key: Mutex<Option<Arc<Frame>>>, inputs: InputLog } with fn publish(&self, region: Rect, enc: Encoding, data: Bytes, keyframe: bool) -> Arc<Frame>, fn republish_keyframe(&self) -> bool and fn stamp(&self, captured_us: u64) -> u64. It is a shared component that replaces 4 hand-rolled broadcasters.

struct RgbaImage { w: u32, h: u32, px: Vec<u8> } with fn blit(&mut self, r: Rect, src: &[u8]) -> Result<(), BlitError>, fn crop(&self, r: Rect) -> Vec<u8>, fn fill(&mut self, r: Rect, rgba: [u8;4]), fn copy_rect(&mut self, from: Rect, to: (u32,u32)). This one pixel buffer replaces the five per-crate versions.

trait RectDecoder { fn encoding(&self) -> i32; async fn decode(&mut self, r: Rect, rd: &mut (dyn AsyncRead + Unpin + Send), fb: &mut RgbaImage) -> Result<Damage>; } plus a registry built from [Raw, CopyRect, Rre, Hextile, Zrle, Cursor, DesktopSize]. ENCODINGS sent to the server is derived from that registry, which removes the duplicate list between proto.rs and surface.rs.

struct DocFormat { kind: Format, mime: &'static str, exts: &'static [&'static str], label: &'static str, sniff: fn(&[u8]) -> bool, open: fn(&[u8], &Fonts) -> Result<Box<dyn Document>> } in a static FORMATS: &[DocFormat] table. It replaces the five Format matches and Parsed::parse/paged.

trait Document: Paged + Send + Sync { fn text(&self) -> String; fn query(&self, q: &DataQuery) -> Option<Result<Value>> { None } } so each format answers its own queries. This removes the 35-line answer() match in docs/server.rs.

trait SurfaceMode { fn update(&mut self, msg: ModeMessage, ctx: &mut TabCtx) -> Task<Message>; fn view<'a>(&'a self, t: &'a dyn SurfaceTheme) -> Element<'a, Message>; fn header_extras(&self) -> Vec<Element<'_, Message>>; fn tab(&self) -> TabSummary; } with PixelMode and DocumentMode in loa-ui-surface. It replaces Body enum matching in about 10 methods of state.rs.

trait FrameDecoder { fn accepts(&self) -> &[Encoding]; fn apply(&mut self, f: &Frame, fb: &mut RgbaImage) -> Result<(), DecodeError>; } as a strategy chain (StillDecoder, plus an optional VideoDecoder adapter only if the video feature survives). Negotiation is computed from the chain.

abstractions: trait KeyStore { fn load(&self) -> Result<Option<SecretBytes>>; fn store(&self, s: &[u8;32]) -> Result<()>; fn delete(&self) -> Result<()>; }. Adapters: MemoryKeyStore, OsKeychain, FileKeyStore. Policy: struct FallbackStore<P: KeyStore, F: KeyStore> { primary: P, fallback: F } which itself implements KeyStore (decorator).

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)] pub struct PublicKey([u8;32]); impl From<PublicKey> for iroh::PublicKey / biscuit_auth::PublicKey / loa_bus::NodeKey. This replaces NodePublicKey, the grant_key/bus_key/node_id helpers and the hand-written trait impls.

struct ResourceKind { name: &'static str, actions: &'static [Action], encode: fn(&Resource) -> String, decode: fn(&str) -> Result<Resource> }. Use static KINDS: [ResourceKind; 8] as a registry, and represent token rights as one Datalog fact right($kind, $key, $action). RULES, right_fact, narrowing_check and token_scopes then each become a single generic loop.

trait Transport: Send + Sync { fn name(&self) -> TransportKind; async fn dial(&self, peer: &NodeId, hints: &[SocketAddr], alpn: &[u8]) -> Result<Connection>; fn close(&self); }. Network becomes FallbackDialer { transports: Vec<Arc<dyn Transport>>, first_timeout: Duration }.

trait Discoverer: Send { async fn next(&mut self) -> Option<NearbyPeer>; fn availability(&self) -> Availability; }. Adapters: MdnsDiscoverer and TailnetDiscoverer<P: NodeProbe>. The node merges them through one note_nearby(NearbyPeer, DiscoverySource).

Generic wire exchange: async fn call<Req: Message, Rep: Message + Default>(stream: &mut Stream, req: Req) -> Result<Rep>, together with trait Envelope { fn ack(err: Option<String>) -> Self; fn into_ack(self) -> Result<Self, NodeError>; }. Every protocol's Frame implements it, which removes the repeated Ack/Refused/expected-X tails.

trait GrantGate { fn live_grants(&self, peer: &NodeId, now: i64) -> Vec<VerifiedGrant>; fn allows(&self, peer, req: &Request, now) -> bool; } is implemented once by GrantAccess. extra.rs covers(), folder.rs covered() and access.rs all call it.

trait PeerProtocol (keep as is) plus a ProtocolRegistry { fn register(&mut self, alpn: Alpn, h: Arc<dyn ProtocolHandler>) }. Control, session and folder register through the same registry that app-added protocols use (sandbox).

trait FeedSource: Send + Sync { async fn fetch(&self, product: &Product, cached: Option<&CachedFeed>) -> Result<FeedResponse>; }. Use a registry keyed by the Feed variant, so Updater::check is a single code path and Watcher goes away.
trait Unpacker { fn unpack(&self, artifact: &Path, payload: &Path) -> Result<()>; }. Strategies: TarGz{strip}, Zip, Raw, all built on a shared EntrySink (dir/file/symlink/hardlink) with confinement.

Gate ports stay in loa-updater: ToolCatalog, FormatProbe, RpcProbe, ContractRunner and ChangelogSummarizer. Their omp-backed adapters live in loa-app on top of loa_omp_rpc::RpcClient. This follows the ARCHITECTURE port rule, since loa-app supplies the implementations.

theming_seam:
All visual values are resolved through one TokenSet that sits behind a ThemeSource trait in loa-ui-kit::theme. Widgets never contain hex colors, alpha literals, radii, font sizes or padding literals. They call role-based lookups: `t.color(ColorRole::Text2)`, `t.size(SizeRole::Small)`, `t.space(SpaceRole::Sm)`, `t.radius(RadiusRole::Card)`, or a style recipe such as `style::button(ButtonKind::Ghost)`, `style::container(Surface::Card)` or `style::text(Tone::Muted)`.

Roles are closed enums with stable string names via `as_str`/`FromStr`. A future theming script can therefore address them by name (for example `button.ghost.hover.bg = text2 @ 0.1`) without touching widget code.

BuiltinTheme provides today's dark and light sets. The iced Palette is derived from the TokenSet (not the reverse), so iced built-in widgets follow the same source.

shell::theme::State owns the current `Arc<dyn ThemeSource>` and the Light/Dark variant, and publishes the active TokenSet to a global registry that style closures read, because iced style fns only receive `&iced::Theme`. It also emits a ThemeChanged event so components holding precomputed looks can rebuild them: chat Look/markdown Settings, the decisions markdown settings and the terminal TermPalette, which must take its ANSI base colors from tokens (TermRole slots) and not hue-rotate the iced palette ad hoc.

Component-level overrides can later be expressed as a `StyleKey` (component, part, state) lookup layered over roles. The recipe functions take that key, so a script can restyle `sidebar.row.selected` without new code.

Icons stay tint-by-role: `icon(Icon, SizeRole, Tone)`.

theming_seams:
Today loa-app has 83 numeric text sizes, 81 numeric paddings and 12 direct colors, and it never calls loa_ui_shell::style::tokens(). The seam should work like this:
1. loa-ui-shell (or the new loa-ui-kit) owns a `ThemeTokens` trait with semantic keys: ColorToken (ground, side, card, raised, text, text2, text3, accent, ok, warn, danger, line, ...), Space (xs/s/m/l/xl, page_gutter), TextRole (title, heading, body, label, caption, mono), Radius, and Layout constants (composer_width, nav_width, window sizes). DARK and LIGHT become one `StaticTokens` implementation. The active implementation is stored as `Arc<dyn ThemeTokens>`, reached from iced's Theme (Theme::Custom carrying the registry) or from Ctx.theme. That gives a future script interpreter one `impl ThemeTokens for ScriptedTheme` adapter to provide, without touching widgets.
2. Widget style functions (card, row, badge, meter, input) take the tokens and are referenced by a WidgetStyle key, so a script can override a whole widget style.
3. loa-app views only compose ui-kit components (Card, SectionHeader, StatusRow, Form, SideNav, Meter) and pass semantic roles. They never pass numbers or colors. The app.rs constants COMPOSER_WIDTH, COMPOSER_INSET, the window sizes in detach.rs and windows.rs, usage WIDTH and sandbox/peers PROMPT_WIDTH/LIST_WIDTH all move to Layout tokens.
4. A CI lint (grep) forbids `.size(<digit>`, `padding(<digit>`, `Color::` and `extended_palette` inside loa-app and the area views.
5. Theme selection (the THEMES table in app.rs:37 and the Preference mapping in app.rs:1421-1438) becomes a ThemeRegistry list of named token sets, so script-defined themes show up in the palette and the settings automatically.
